newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end 2.8 pct down on Rao case reports.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end 2.8 pct down on Rao case reports.

text.p: Delhi shares fell 20.43 points or 2.8 percent on nervous selling by operators, triggered by speculations about the court's decision on P.V. Narasimha Rao in the St Kitts case, brokers said.
The Delhi bourse's benchmark index closed at 695.56. On Thursday it closed at 715.99.
"Expectations of fresh development against P.V. Narasimha Rao in St Kitts case kept the market depressed throughout the session," said Suresh Aggarwala of brokers Jaimata Securities.

Later in the day, a Delhi judge issued a warrant ordering Rao to appear in court later this month to face forgery charges in the case involving alleged falsification of papers on an illegal bank account in the Carribean island to defame former Prime Minister V.P. Singh.
Singh alleged that he was defamed seven years ago, when he was leading an anti-corruption campaign against Rao's Congress party government.
Reliance Industries fell 0.05 rupee to 191 while Larsen nad Toubro was down five rupees to 225.0 in linewith the market sentiments.
State Bank of India lost 10.25 rupees at 231.15 and TISCO ended one rupee lower at 171.90.
